identity.description: Google's NotebookLM, sold as NotebookLM Enterprise / Gemini Notebook Enterprise inside Google Cloud and Gemini Enterprise. The consumer notebooklm.google.com product is not covered by these API docs.
identity.identity_notes: Google Cloud docs describe NotebookLM Enterprise and its newer name Gemini Notebook Enterprise. Matches the assigned Gemini Enterprise API surface. The official overview page was fetched; the naming change is confirmed by the page title variants.

auth.oauth_flows: unknown. Docs show a bearer token from gcloud auth print-access-token under user sign-in; they do not name OAuth 2.0 explicitly.
auth.scopes_notes: No scopes documented on pages checked. Drive-based sources need Google user credentials with Drive access enabled at gcloud login.

api.limitations: Covers notebook management (create, get, list recently viewed, share, batch delete) and source management (batch add, single file upload, get, batch delete). No chat, audio, or content-generation endpoints found in the pages checked. Calling user needs a Gemini Notebook Enterprise license. Uses the v1alpha surface. Consumer NotebookLM API availability not established.

open_questions: Trial length conflict: Cloud docs say 14-day, 5000-license trial; a localized product page reportedly says 30-day trial then $9/license/month (min 15). Not resolved; verify on live pricing page.
Rate limits: a search snippet mentions 500 queries per notebook per day; not verified on a fetched page.
No Google-published MCP server found. The Cloud API docs do not mention MCP, SDKs, or webhooks.
Whether a Google-maintained client library exists for the v1alpha notebooks API is unknown.
Whether the consumer notebooklm.google.com product has any public API is not established by these sources.

Community repos (jacob-bd, roomi-fields, PyPI packages) were not fetched; their use of internal/unofficial APIs is from search snippets only. Their Enterprise support is described as experimental in one snippet.

rationale: Self-serve test credentials (trial self serve) and a documented REST interface.
API surface is limited; toolkit would cover few actions.
